messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] PC prior for
parts:
Karim,

congratulations, you're the first to request this feature and you have
prepared a good case for why this is a sensible thing to do!!!

This is work in progress and we're not there yet. there will be more
progress on this later this year and next year, so I'm sorry, what you
ask for is not possible as it is now.

Best,
H


On Thu, 2015-02-05 at 14:30 -0800, 'Karim Anaya-Izquierdo' via R-inla
discussion group wrote:
> Dear R-INLA list,
>
>
> I have data which can be modelled as follows
>
>
> n = 100
> prec.1=1
> prec.2=5
> nb = 4
> nz1 = 5
> nz2 = 10
> Z1 = kronecker(diag(nz1),rep(1,20))
> Z2 = matrix(runif(n*nz2), n, nz2)
> b1 = rnorm(nz1,mean=0,sd=1/sqrt(prec.1))
> b2 = rnorm(nz2,mean=0,sd=1/sqrt(prec.2))
> beta = 5 + rnorm(nb)
> X = matrix(runif(n*nb), n, nb)
> X[,1] = 1
> eta = X %*% beta + Z1 %*% b1 + Z2 %*% b2
> y = eta + rnorm(n, sd=0.01)
>
>
> formula = y ~ -1 + X + f(id.z1, model="z", Z=Z1)+f(id.z2, model="z",
> Z=Z2)
> result = inla(formula, data = list(y=y, id.z1 = 1:n,id.z2 = 1:n, X=X))
>
>
> so there are 2 random effects: one that describes some sort of
> clustering and another one that is spatial (although I omitted the
> spatial aspect in the above example).
> The main point is that I am interesting in a base model (or standard
> model) which is the one with only the cluster random effects, that is
> eta = X %*% beta + Z1 %*% b1.
> The model with two random effects is a generalization of the base
> model which I would use only if the base model does not fit the data
> well!
>
>
> My question is if it is possible to adapt the bym2 model described in
>
>
> http://inla.googlecode.com/hg-history/475192f4b6f3668d2637e54547517b3747082e16/r-inla.org/doc/latent/bym2.pdf
>
>
>
> to my situation? or perhaps using a different latent model in terms
> the model "z" or something like that. If this is the case, is it
> possible to apply the PC-priors of Simpson, Martins et al to my
> situation by using something similar to the code described in
>
>
> http://www.math.ntnu.no/inla/r-inla.org/case-studies/Martins-etal-2014/bym/bym.R
>
>
> ?
>
>
>
> Thanks in advance
>
>
> Karim
